name: Ursula Bechtolsheimer-Kipp
current_role: Chairwoman (board president), Tschuggen Hotel Group / Tschuggen Collection (since 2016; current status not reconfirmed)
profile: German-born heiress (b. 1951), only daughter of Karl-Heinz Kipp, founder of the Massa department-store chain whose real estate was leased to Metro. She inherited much of his fortune in 2017 and chairs the family's Swiss luxury hotel group (Tschuggen Grand & Valsana Arosa, Carlton St. Moritz, Eden Roc Ascona). Lived for decades in Gloucestershire, running a horse breeding centre; now reported resident in Switzerland.
interesting_fact: The family fortune began with 500 bottles of rare wine her father sold on the post-war black market; her daughter is Olympic dressage gold medallist Laura Tomlinson.
deep_cut_fact: In 2016, alongside taking the Tschuggen chair from her 92-year-old father, she also became chair of Swiss property company Gassmann Immobilien- und Beteiligungs-AG and backed the Massa Nova project in Chur with her son Götz (per Bilanz).

public_contacts.value: c.maerzheuser@tschuggencollection.ch (Constanze Märzheuser, Director of PR, Tschuggen Collection)

notes: Very private; no personal social accounts found. Best route is the Tschuggen Collection PR director. Husband Wilfried died 2020 (avoid). Was dropped from Forbes real-time list after 2021.

name: Dmitry Pumpansky
current_role: Former owner and chairman of TMK (Russian steel-pipe maker); left TMK's board and beneficial ownership in March 2022
profile: Russian industrialist (b. 1964, usually spelled Dmitry Pumpyansky), graduate of the Ural Polytechnic Institute. Started as a metals trader, ran pipe plants including Sinarsky, joined TMK in 2002 and by 2006 owned 100% of it, building one of the world's largest makers of oil-and-gas tubulars. Said to have exited TMK in 2022; reported living in Geneva.
interesting_fact: After co-buying TMK with Sergei Popov and Andrey Melnichenko, he bought both partners out in 2006 to become its sole owner.
deep_cut_fact: In 2024 he earned a Doctor of Technical Sciences degree with a dissertation on steels, alloys and production technologies for next-generation OCTG and specialty pipes, adding to his earlier engineering candidate degree and economics doctorate.
notes: Name in input is a variant spelling of Pumpyansky. Sanctioned by UK (2022) and named on the US CAATSA list; EU sanctions annulled by the EU General Court on appeal. Outreach carries compliance/reputational risk; no published personal or office contact found.

name: Maurizio Billi
current_role: Controlling shareholder and chairman/president of Eurofarma (Brazilian pharma group)
profile: Son of Italian chemist Galliano Billi, who founded Eurofarma in 1972. Maurizio joined as a teenager, took over as president in 2000 and turned it into one of Brazil's largest drugmakers, expanding via acquisitions across Latin America (operations in 20+ countries, 12,600+ staff). Still leads the company and its strategy.
interesting_fact: An avid racer: his Eurofarma team has repeatedly won Stock Car Brasil titles, and in 2013 he himself won a race in the Porsche Master Cup Brasil.
deep_cut_fact: He was born in 1957, the same year his parents emigrated from Italy to South America, and at 19 (1976) started helping his father's small company, rotating through production, finance, purchasing and HR before becoming president in 2000.
notes: Described by Forbes Brasil as discreet. No published press email found; Eurofarma site blocks scraping. Sources differ on title (president vs chairman of the board); company 2024 report signs him as Presidente do Conselho.

name: Antonio Del Valle Ruiz
current_role: Honorary Chairman for Life, Orbia Advance Corp. (ex-Mexichem); patriarch of Grupo Kaluz
profile: Mexico City-born banker-turned-industrialist (b. 1938). After Mexico's 1982 bank nationalisation and later reprivatisation he built Grupo Financiero Bital, then swapped a bank stake for control of Mexichem, now Orbia, a global maker of plastic pipes, fluorochemicals and PVC. The family holds ~46% of Orbia plus Banco Ve por Más, Elementia/Fortaleza and Chicago's Byline Bank via Grupo Kaluz; his children run day-to-day.
interesting_fact: He founded and funds Museo Kaluz in Mexico City's historic centre (opened Oct 2020 in the former Hotel de Cortés), showing his ~1,800-piece collection of Mexican art (Velasco, Rivera, Siqueiros, Orozco) built over five decades, which he called a gift to the country.
deep_cut_fact: His Fundación Del Valle bought the historic Hotel de Cortés building on Avenida Hidalgo in 2013 and restored it from 2016; its façade now carries Vicente Rojo's mural 'Jardín Urbano', with tree-like forms chosen because so much of the collection is landscape painting.
notes: Aged 88; children (e.g. Antonio del Valle Perochena, Kaluz chairman) run the businesses. For energy/industrial angle, Orbia's corporate communications/IR is the alternative route. Museum press office is the warmest public channel tied to him personally.

name: William Hockey
current_role: Co-founder and co-CEO, Column N.A. (developer-focused nationally chartered bank); board member, Plaid
profile: Emory history/business grad who met Zach Perret as a junior Bain consultant and co-founded Plaid in 2012, the API layer connecting fintech apps to bank accounts. Left as CTO/president in 2019 and, with his wife Annie, bought a small California bank and relaunched it in 2022 as Column, a self-funded chartered bank powering fintechs such as Brex and Mercury.
interesting_fact: Rather than seek a de novo charter, he and Annie bought 94.1% of Chico-based Northern California National Bank for about $45 million in July 2021 and renamed it Column National Association that August.
deep_cut_fact: The bank he bought was a small community lender whose CEO Todd Lewis was kept on in a leadership role under the 2021 tender-offer terms, so Column's charter traces back to a Chico, California community bank.
notes: Low public profile; personal X/LinkedIn handle not verified. Column press inbox is the best route; engineering-heavy fintech/banking-infrastructure angle.

name: Laura Love
current_role: Co-owner (with siblings Greg, Frank and Jenny) of Love's Travel Stops & Country Stores; no public executive role found
profile: One of four children of Tom and Judy Love, who founded Love's in Oklahoma in 1964 with a $5,000 loan from Tom's parents. The family-owned chain now runs 600+ truck stops and convenience stores in 42 states with ~$22B estimated sales; brothers Greg and Frank are co-CEOs and sister Jenny Love Meyer is chief culture officer. Laura keeps a very low public profile.
interesting_fact: Love's began in 1964 when Tom and Judy Love started it with a $5,000 loan from Tom's parents; it remains wholly family-owned with 600+ locations in 42 states.
notes: Very private; no interviews, personal accounts or individual role found. Parents died 2023 (Tom) and 2024 (Judy) - avoid. A podcast pitch would more realistically go to the co-CEOs via the company media group.

name: Bang Si-hyuk
current_role: Founder and Chairman of the Board, HYBE Co. (formerly Big Hit Entertainment)
profile: Seoul National University aesthetics graduate and hit songwriter ('Hitman Bang') who co-founded JYP Entertainment's songwriting engine before launching Big Hit, home of BTS. HYBE's 2020 IPO made him a billionaire; it has since bought Ithaca Holdings and built a multi-label global group. He stepped down as CEO in 2021 and remains chairman.
interesting_fact: He signed RM, later BTS's leader, when RM was just 15, and co-wrote six songs on BTS's 2016 album 'Wings'.
deep_cut_fact: He debuted as a composer while still a student, winning the 1994 Yoo Jae-ha Music Contest; in 2022 SNU gave him an honorary business doctorate, the first awarded to an entertainment-industry figure.
notes: Ongoing criminal investigation over 2019-20 pre-IPO dealings (case referred to prosecutors Sept 2026; shares provisionally seized) - outreach timing/reputational sensitivity. No verified published press email found (press@hybecorp.com appears only in third-party docs, not used). Route via HYBE corporate communications.

name: David C Paul
current_role: Founder and Executive Chairman, Globus Medical (NYSE: GMED)
profile: Mechanical engineer who left Synthes, where he was Director of Product Development, to found spine and musculoskeletal device maker Globus Medical in 2003. He was CEO until 2017, then executive chairman; he remains the largest stockholder after Globus' 2023 merger with NuVasive, and Keith Pfeil has been CEO since July 2025.
interesting_fact: He is named as an inventor on more than 300 patents and published patent applications.
deep_cut_fact: Before industry he was a research engineer in biomaterials at Temple University. He earned a mechanical engineering degree from the University of Madras in India and a master's in computer-integrated mechanical engineering systems from Temple.

public_contacts.value: investors@globusmedical.com (Brian Kearns, SVP Corporate Development & IR)

notes: Engineer-founder; low media profile. Also sits on boards of Free Flow Medical and Cross Ventures LLC (real estate). Company IR is the published route.

name: David Booth
current_role: Co-founder and Executive Chairman, Dimensional Fund Advisors
profile: Lawrence, Kansas native (KU econ BA/MS) who studied under Eugene Fama at the University of Chicago, worked on one of the first index funds at Wells Fargo, then co-founded Dimensional with Rex Sinquefield in 1981 to apply academic research to low-cost, systematic investing. Dimensional manages hundreds of billions of dollars; Booth is a Giving Pledge signer and major University of Chicago donor.
interesting_fact: He paid $4.3 million for James Naismith's original 1891 rules of basketball, now displayed at the University of Kansas; his 2008 $300M gift to the University of Chicago is the largest in its history (hence Chicago Booth).
deep_cut_fact: He grew up in a house just down the street from KU's Allen Fieldhouse. After serving as Fama's teaching assistant he skipped academia, reasoning of Fama: 'He was smarter than I was and willing to work harder.'

public_contacts.value: Has appeared on podcasts e.g. Rational Reminder ep. 131 (guest, not his own show)

notes: Relatively accessible: has done long-form podcast interviews about the first index fund. Dimensional media relations is the published route.
